$comment: Kiln's install for this frame, as data. `device`: what Kiln's device flows read (kiln-core DeviceFrame): its names, board, release line, timings, assets, the browser storage it keeps, and its words. Format: docs/design/kiln/frames-as-data.md. A draft (#621): the contract (kiln/apps/kiln/test/contract) reads route, touch and each step's id, writes, reboots, downloads and taps; the engine reads the rest from phase 2.

enter.why: VOL- is on a board inside the case. On the Glass Panes image the Mirror runs adb, so phase 2 enters fastboot with adb reboot bootloader.
VOL- is on a board inside the case, and stock lululemon software has no adb Kiln can use: the back cover comes off once, and stays off until the second fastboot
VOL- again, with the back cover still off

wayBack.why: The restore point Kiln keeps before the install puts back every block of system it changed, from the Mirror's own bytes

connect.title: Connect to your Mirror
connect.body: Plug it into this computer over micro-USB, with Glassworks running.

listed.why: The name Chrome's USB list shows the Mirror by, over adb and in fastboot alike: nobody finds "the Mirror" there (maintainer, 2026-11-21). Kiln's screens say it wherever they ask for a pick, and set-up's sheet names it

apk.why: Glassworks' legacy build, for Android 6; its CPU runs 64-bit apps (frame.json abis)

timings.why: authMs: how long the keep step waits for the Mirror to let this browser's adb key in (a Mirror that trusts another browser's key waits for a tap it can't take); firstStartAuthMs: the first start's first try, longer since a Mirror that just restarted takes its time (PR 607); readMs: one read over adb

assets.why: branding/lululemon-mirror/bootanimation.zip and frames/lululemon-mirror/overlay/GlassworksSettings.apk (Wi-Fi on, no screen timeout, no lock screen, no auto-rotate), staged with Kiln's other assets

storage.why: flashedFlag, localStorage: this browser has flashed a Mirror (issue 580). inPlaceDb, IndexedDB: the bundles and restore points of in-place installs (Stock-in-place). Browsers hold both: never rename

words.image.vendor: Its vendor files come from Qualcomm and Quectel, via the Glass Panes release.
words.image.lede: Kiln adds Glassworks to the Glass Panes system image and writes it over USB.
words.fastboot.restarted: The Mirror is restarting into fastboot mode. Click Connect and pick `Android`.
words.fastboot.byHandSteps:
Switch the Mirror off with the rocker switch in its bottom edge, unplug its power cord, and lay it face down.
Remove the 4 screws in the bottom edge and lift off the stand. Remove the 14 screws in the back (including 2 on either side of the recess by the feet) and lift off the back cover.
Plug the power cord back into its socket in that recess, keeping the switch off.
Connect the micro-USB port near the top corner to this computer.
On the small green board at the top end, press and hold VOL− (SW3) — the one of its two buttons closer to the top edge.
Keep holding while you switch the Mirror on, and for about 5 seconds more. The screen will stay dark, which is normal.
words.fastboot.byHandNote: Hold only VOL−, since pressing VOL+ or both buttons starts other modes. Some Mirrors have a small service hatch on the back that lets you reach the board without removing the whole cover.
words.fastboot.overUsb: Already running Glassworks or Glass Panes? Restart over USB
words.confirm.title: This replaces lululemon’s software for good
words.confirm.lede: The Mirror's bootloader can't read its original software back, so Kiln can't create a backup before replacing it. You can always return to the plain Glass Panes image from Kiln.
words.confirm.understand: I understand lululemon's original software can't be restored.
words.adb.firstStart: The screen stays dark for a few minutes on first boot — that's normal. Leave it plugged in, click Connect, and pick `Android`.
words.done.noTouch: Because the Mirror has no touchscreen, hide the other launcher again or plug in a USB mouse to choose Glassworks, then Always.
words.done.noHomeFix: Install a build of Glassworks made for Android 6 over USB.
words.error.noFill: If the write failed on a sparse chunk, try compatibility write mode below — it transfers about 200 MB more, which works around older bootloaders.
words.keep.steps: Plug the Mirror's micro-USB cable into this computer with Glassworks running.
words.community.ifVendor: If the Mirror still runs lululemon's software, that original software can't be restored afterward.
words.app.pick.release: Kiln installs the latest Glassworks release over USB and sets it as the Mirror's only home screen.
words.app.pick.local: Choose the legacy build of Glassworks for Android. Kiln will set it as the Mirror's only home screen.
words.app.connectHelp: Plug the Mirror into this computer, click Connect, and select it in the list. Then choose **Allow** on the Mirror using a USB mouse.
words.fastboot.notLetIn: The Mirror didn't allow this browser to connect — it may still run lululemon's software, or Glassworks installed from another browser. Put it into fastboot mode using the steps above.
words.inPlace.stage.lede: Kiln keeps lululemon's system and changes only the parts Glassworks needs. First it adds a small setup agent to the Mirror's app storage, so it can read those parts back.
words.inPlace.receive.lede: The Mirror is restarting into the setup agent, which takes a minute or two. The screen may stay dark. Leave it plugged in with the back cover still off.
words.inPlace.receive.waiting: Waiting for the Mirror to start its setup agent
words.inPlace.receive.lan: Getting it over your local network
words.inPlace.receive.ble: Getting it over Bluetooth. This takes about five minutes, so keep this computer near the Mirror.
words.inPlace.receive.file: Open the Mirror's download page, save the bundle, then pick it here.
words.inPlace.restorePoint.lede: Before it changes anything in the system, Kiln keeps the exact parts it will change, from your Mirror's own copy. They're saved in this browser, and you can download a copy too.
words.inPlace.confirm.lede: Kiln writes the setup agent to the Mirror's app storage now. lululemon's system isn't touched yet, and nothing in it changes until you've saved a restore point.
words.inPlace.appInstall.lede: Kiln installs Glassworks, hides lululemon's apps, and lets Glassworks install its own updates.
words.inPlace.wayBack: To go back, Kiln writes the restore point over the parts it changed, putting lululemon's system back as it was. The Mirror's app data starts fresh either way.
words.inPlace.fastboot.again: Put the Mirror in fastboot mode once more: switch it off with the rocker switch, press and hold VOL− (SW3) on the small green board, and keep holding while you switch it on, then for about 5 seconds more. Keep the back cover off until the install is done.
words.inPlace.coverNote: Keep the back cover off until the install is done: you'll need VOL− once more.
words.inPlace.changes: The Mirror's app data starts fresh, while lululemon's system stays in place. Only the parts Kiln saved in the restore point change, so you can always go back.
words.inPlace.startOver: Kiln adds the setup agent again, and the Mirror's app data starts fresh again. lululemon's system stays as it is.

on.line: Updates from Home Assistant install automatically in the background.

normal-app.line: Android asks before each update, which needs a USB mouse since the Mirror has no touchscreen. Installing over fastboot makes updates automatic.

not-granted.line: Android didn't let Glassworks install its own updates automatically, so each one asks first. Reinstalling the image fixes this.

unknown.line: Kiln couldn't read this back — check Settings → Device on the Mirror to see its status.

install.text: Android is installing and optimizing it
Start Glassworks for the first time
Set as the only home screen

needs: On a first install from lululemon's software, a screwdriver for the back cover
picker.wayBack: The Mirror's bootloader can't read its software back, so there is no backup. Kiln can always install the plain Glass Panes image instead.
picker.why: The picker's What you'll need bar (#672), as the frame's README and its fastboot steps say it
